sentences.text: Sapeornis was a small bird measuring between 30 and 33 centimeters in length when alive, a measurement that excludes its tail feathers.
Its skull possessed only a few teeth located strictly at the very tip of the upper jaw.
The animal featured tail feathers arranged into a graded, fan-like structure.
The humerus was large and contained holes designed to reduce weight, a trait similar to that seen in Confuciusornithidae.
Unlike modern birds with long bony tails, Sapeornis had a rod-like pygostyle.
The first toe of its foot pointed backwards.
Its reduced fingers suggest the presence of an alula, a structure used for flight control.
The hand was far more advanced than that of Archaeopteryx, featuring three fingers with specific phalange counts and a carpometacarpus.
Arms were one and a half times longer than the legs, indicating a large wing area.
The skeleton included gastralia, though it lacked ossified uncinate processes.
A preserved specimen contained numerous small gastroliths within its stomach area.
Evidence points to Sapeornis being a glider or soarer that preferred open country but could perch on branches.
Fossil evidence suggests it was a herbivore that ate plant seeds and fruits, utilizing diverse food resources.
The first specimen was found in the summer of 2000 near Chaoyang City in Liaoning Province, China.
It was discovered by the IVPP and reported in 2002 by scientists Zhonghe Zhou and Fucheng Zhang.
Two more nearly complete specimens were later found about 40 km from the original site in the Dapingfang area.
The genus name honors the Society of Avian Paleontology and Evolution combined with the Greek word for bird.
Analysis of skeletal bones suggests Sapeornis had slow growth similar to Archaeopteryx, unlike the rapid growth of modern birds.
Sapeornis is classified within the class Aves.
It belongs to the order Omnivoropterygiformes and the family Omnivoropterygidae.
The species belongs to the parent group Pygostylia.
A 2012 study concluded that Didactylornis, Shenshiornis, and S. angustis are synonyms of Sapeornis chaoyangensis, and Omnivoropteryx is probably also another synonym.
Sapeornis lived during the early Cretaceous period, approximately 125 to 120 million years ago.
Other data indicate it lived from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 113.2 million years ago.
Character analysis demonstrates that Sapeornis was not closely related to Confuciusornis despite sharing some derived features.
